author: GamingBolt
description:
Disgaea Mayhem is a tricky one. On the one hand, it's an ambitious effort to breach new frontiers from its developers, and manages to do that with mixed results. On the other hand, its very simplicity makes it fall prey to a repetitive gameplay loop that threatens to alienate players when it should be drawing them in for more.

Does it manage to find a balance between the two? Well, we dived into a full review, and tried out everything it has to offer to answer that very question. Join us as we take you through this fun offering from Nippon Ichi, and try to help you decide if it's worth picking up.
title: Disgaea Mayhem Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
Promoting Xbox Series X/S growth is tough, and that's before getting into price hikes and console shortages. Removing day-one first-party titles may also have a knock-on effect for PC. The majority sticks to Steam when it comes to purchasing titles, after all. One would assume that there's some kind of crossover coming with Project Helix to allow for playing your Steam games on the platform, balancing it out with Game Pass. But again, if it sounds too good to be true, so on and so forth.

Aside from introducing that rumored free Cloud Gaming tier supported by advertising, Game Pass is a paradox for Xbox. It can't be trifled with too much, lest it runs the risk of losing more subscribers, but it can't be left alone at the risk of no growth. So while it won't be sunset anytime soon, you have to wonder if those discussions are at least being explored, if not entertained. Regardless, even if Xbox opts to slay the albatross and move on, it won't stop weighing on the company any time soon.
title: Does Game Pass NEED to Die for Xbox to Survive?

author: GamingBolt
description:
After Gears of War: Reloaded and Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 planted their flags in PlayStation territory, Halo remained steadfast as Xbox’s last bastion of exclusivity to cross the divide. 

That was until Halo: Campaign Evolved emerged late last year, a ground-up remake of Master Chief’s seminal debut primed for Sony’s home console. And, at the time, this felt like the culminating first wave of Microsoft’s multi-platform ‘Project Latitude’ strategy. The expectation was, now the walls were well and truly down, that platform exclusivity will become increasingly rare, and that Microsoft’s ‘Play Anywhere’ strategy really did mean anywhere.
title: Could Halo Campaign Evolved Be PlayStation’s First And Last Halo?
